title: Recorder, retention & disk budget
body:
## Context
CandleViewer can only ever analyse order flow it recorded itself: Bybit exposes no historical L2, no historical liquidations and only a ~1000-row recent-trade window (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md#13-recorder-retention-and-replay`). Every R2 surface (footprint E18, profiles E19, Deep-Stats E20, CVD E23, replay E26) is exactly as deep as this recorder has been running, which is why `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.1 schedules E16 in **S06–S07** rather than at the end of the R1 train.

Recording everything is simple and wrong: ~0.5–0.75 GB/day/symbol compressed at 200 depth (budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`) fills a personal machine in weeks. Owner decision #4 therefore locks: a user-managed recorded-symbol list **empty by default**, auto-record on open chart / open position, 30-day default retention, pin = keep forever, and a visible disk budget. Security area 8 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8) rates unbounded recording a **Critical** DoS against the trading host.

Backend modules: **M10 Recorder** (`RecordingPolicy`, `StreamWriter`, `RetentionManager`, `RollOffJob`, `DiskBudget` — `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) and **M11** storage tiering/roll-off into the Parquet lake (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5–§7).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories US-REC-001 … US-REC-008 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#22-rec--recording--retention`).
- Postgres migration `0007_recorder`: `recorded_symbols`, `recording_sessions`, `recording_gaps`, `retention_policies` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6).
- REST: `/recording/symbols`, `/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}`, `…/pin`, `/recording/status`, `/recording/storage`, `/recording/retention-policies`, `/recording/sessions`, `/market/data-coverage`, `/admin/recorder/compact`, `/admin/recorder/purge`.
- WS topic `recorder` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.8 `RecorderUpdate`), and the `no_data_recorded` topic warning contract.
- Screens SCR-140 (Admin: recorder & storage), SCR-141 (retention policy editor), SCR-142 (storage & database panel), SCR-047 (chart empty/no-data), SCR-151 (empty-state pattern).
- Components CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow, CMP-026 EmptyState (`variant="recording-not-started"`), CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-049 Table, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Jobs: nightly verified hot→cold export, weekly compactor, retention reaper with dry-run, disk-pressure ladder, bulk archive importer.
- Observability: `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `disk_used_ratio`; audit actions `recorder.start|stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Out of scope
- The replay engine and scrubbing UI (E26, R2) — E16 only guarantees the data and the coverage metadata replay consumes.
- Footprint/profile/CVD aggregate computation (E18/E19/E23); E16 records the raw tape those are rebuilt from.
- Android or any non-web client; a separate admin app (admin screens live inside the web app, RBAC-gated).
- Non-Bybit exchanges and non-USDT-perp instruments.
- Backups/restore (`/admin/backups/*`) — owned by the platform/ops epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fresh install records nothing
  Given a freshly migrated installation
  When the owner opens /admin/recorder
  Then the recorded-symbol list is empty and no market data beyond klines is persisted

Scenario: Seven-day soak with retention and pinning
  Given three symbols recorded continuously for seven days, one of them pinned
  When the nightly retention reaper and the hot->cold export have run each night
  Then past-retention non-pinned partitions are gone from QuestDB and present in Parquet with verified checksums
  And no pinned partition has been deleted at either tier
  And the disk projection shown on SCR-140 is within +/-15% of measured actual growth

Scenario: Disk pressure never silently degrades recording
  Given free space on the data volume falls below 5%
  When the disk-budget guard evaluates
  Then recording for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, a critical system event is raised and pinned data is untouched

Scenario: Gaps are honest
  Given the recorder was down for 12 minutes for BTCUSDT
  When any dependent view queries that window
  Then an explicit recording_gaps interval is returned and rendered as a hatched region, never interpolated
```

## Technical notes / design
Effective recorded set = explicit list ∪ open-chart symbols ∪ open-position symbols, per `RecordingPolicy` in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §13.1. Auto-record starts within 2 s of a chart opening (after a 60 s open-dwell guard) and lingers `linger_minutes` (default 15) after the last reason disappears; a symbol with an open position can never stop recording. Writes are batched QuestDB ILP (10k rows / 200 ms) with a bounded 1 GB on-disk WAL spill when QuestDB is unavailable. Trades and book deltas are **never** dropped under backpressure; tickers/klines may be dropped, counted and recorded as a gap. Retention resolution order: pinned → symbol-scoped policy → default policy → hard 30-day default. No hot partition is dropped before its Parquet counterpart is written, SHA-256'd and row-count-verified.

Config/flags: `recorder.auto_record` (default true), `storage.cold_tier` (true), `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` (500). Error codes: `no_data_recorded` (422/WS warning), `resource_purged` (410), `conflict` (409 on un-recording a symbol with an active trigger).

## Test plan
Unit (≥85% on `backend/recorder/*`, `backend/storage/*`): policy resolution, retention resolution, gap detection, projection math, importer parsing. Contract: OpenAPI + `RecorderUpdate` schema conformance. Integration (`03-testing-strategy.md` §5): auto-record trigger → QuestDB write → retention/pin → Parquet roll-off → DuckDB query of rolled-off data. E2E Playwright + Electron over SCR-140/141/142. Perf/soak: 7-day continuous recorder soak on ≥3 symbols; 24 h ingestion soak with zero dropped messages. Chaos: disk at 85/91/96 %, QuestDB down (WAL spill + replay), WS disconnect mid-session.

## Security notes
STRIDE area 8 (`04-security-program.md` §5.8): S2 disk-exhaustion DoS (SR-096), S3 path traversal via archive/export paths (SR-097), S5 retention deleting pinned data (SR-099), S1 silent Parquet corruption (SR-094), S6 exposed QuestDB/DuckDB consoles (SR-048). Purge requires an elevated session, typed `confirm_symbol` echo and a reason; all destructive runs audited (`retention.purge`). Data classification: market data is non-PII operational data; `added_by` links to a user id.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-140/141/142 are WCAG 2.2 AA: disk meters carry numeric text (never bar-only), gap lists are tables with start/end/duration, state is a word not a colour, destructive confirms are focus-trapped dialogs with typed confirmation, and the recorder-dependent empty state is heading + paragraph + real button.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #5 zero undetected dropped messages per symbol over 24 h; #12 storage growth tracked at ≤0.75 GB/day/symbol planning figure; SCR-140 status at 1 Hz must never block ingestion; storage figures sampled server-side every 60 s. Retention/compaction run off-peak (02:15 / 03:00 UTC) and skip partitions referenced by active replay sessions.

## Observability
Prometheus: `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `recorder_dropped_messages_total{symbol,stream}`, `disk_used_ratio`, `retention_deleted_rows_total`, `archive_verify_failures_total`. Alerts at `disk_used_ratio > 0.8`, any `dropped_messages > 0`, any archive verification failure. Audit: `recorder.start`, `recorder.stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion #6 demonstrated: ≥7 continuous days on ≥3 symbols, reaper deletes past-retention data, never touches pinned data, projection within ±15 %.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85 % backend recorder/storage packages, ≥80 % frontend recorder screens.
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0015 reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] axe-core clean on SCR-140/141/142 + manual screen-reader pass.
- [ ] STRIDE area 8 finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass recorded; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review against staging.

## Dependencies
- **E07** storage-tier spike/ADR-0003 — QuestDB + Parquet layout must be settled before the writer and roll-off are built.
- **E08** Bybit adapter & ingestion — the recorder writes the normalized event stream E08 produces.
- **E17** WS protocol — the `recorder` topic and the `no_data_recorded` warning ride the E17 framing.
- **E09** auth/RBAC — `recording:read` / `recording:write` permissions and step-up for purge.
- **E05/E10** design system + app shell — AdminLayout and primitives used by SCR-140/141/142.

## Branch

title: UX research: recorder mental model, auto-record surprise and disk anxiety
body:
## Context
Owner decision #4 makes recording opt-in and empty by default, with silent auto-record on chart/position open. ADR-0015 explicitly names two UX risks as "negative consequences": (a) users will want history for a symbol they only just started recording and it will not exist, and (b) auto-record on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols. Both are UX problems, not engineering problems, and they must be resolved before SCR-140/141/142 wireframes are drawn (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated walkthrough with the Owner and both account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) on: what they expect "recording" to mean, what they expect to happen when they open a chart for a new symbol, and what disk figure they would act on.
- Concept test of three auto-record disclosure options: (1) silent + badge, (2) 60 s dwell then a toast with an undo, (3) explicit prompt on first open per symbol.
- Concept test of two disk-budget framings: "GB used / cap" vs "days of runway at current rate" (both are available from `GET /api/v1/recording/storage`: `daily_growth_bytes`, `projected_full_at`).
- Comprehension test of the recorder-dependent empty state copy ("History starts <ts> — recording began then") used by SCR-047/SCR-151 and every R2 view.
- Written findings doc + a ranked recommendation per question, attached to this ticket and linked from SCR-140 in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
- Producing wireframes or hi-fi screens (E16-D02..D05).
- Testing replay UX (E26).
- Quantitative analytics instrumentation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Auto-record disclosure decided
  Given three auto-record disclosure options were tested with at least three participants
  When findings are written up
  Then one option is recommended with the reasoning and the dissenting evidence recorded
  And the recommendation names the dwell/grace values it assumes (default 60 s dwell, 15 min linger)

Scenario: Disk framing decided
  When participants are shown both disk framings and asked which figure they would act on
  Then the findings state which framing is primary on SCR-140 and which is secondary

Scenario: Empty-state copy comprehension fails safely
  Given a participant misreads the "history starts" copy as an error
  Then the finding is logged as a blocking copy issue and a revised string is proposed and re-tested
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the real API shapes so the stimuli are truthful: `RecordedSymbol` (`reason`, `pinned`, `started_at`, `disk_bytes`, `retention_days`) and `StorageUsage` (`disk_used_bytes`, `daily_growth_bytes`, `projected_full_at`). Stimuli may be static; no build required. Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored on the tailnet only.

## Test plan
N/A (research ticket). Validation is peer review of the findings doc by the Chief Design Officer and the Architect.

## Security notes
Session recordings may show symbol names and account labels — store on the tailnet, never in a public tracker. No API keys, balances or PII in stimuli. Data classification: internal.

## Accessibility notes
At least one participant session run with a screen reader or keyboard-only, so the empty-state and disk-meter copy is validated non-visually.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings doc written, reviewed by CDO and Architect, linked from this ticket.
- [ ] One recommendation per research question, with evidence.
- [ ] Recommendations folded into the SCR-140/141/142 entries in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (or a delta noted).
- [ ] E16-D02 unblocked; no open question remains that would change the SCR-140 layout.

## Dependencies
`E05` design system v0 supplies the visual language the stimuli are drawn in.

## Branch
`design/e16-recorder-research` (docs only). PR ≤400 LOC of markdown.

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md (negative consequences)
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-140, SCR-047, SCR-151
- docs/plan/10-personas.md

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Design SCR-140 recorder & storage screen and CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow
body:
## Context
SCR-140 `/admin/recorder` is the control surface for the whole epic and is also step 4 of onboarding (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-140 and the onboarding wizard). It must make three things impossible to misread: nothing is recorded by default, what auto-record added and why, and what recording costs in disk. `retention.default_changed {before, after}`, `retention.symbol_override_set {symbol, before, after}`, `retention.pin_changed`, `retention.compaction_started|completed`.

title: Spike S6: measure real GB/day per stream for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
body:
## Context
Every retention default, the hot-tier window and `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` currently rest on an unverified first-principles estimate of 0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol compressed at 200 depth (budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, ADR-0015 "Validation", which names this spike **S6**). ADR-0015 states plainly that the estimate "may be off by 2-3x" and makes measurement a precondition for finalising retention defaults. If the constant is wrong, E16 either wastes the volume or prunes data the owner wanted kept - both are user-visible failures that cannot be undone.

This spike measures; it does not build product. Its deliverable is a number per stream, per symbol, per depth tier, good enough to set the constants `E16-T06` and `E16-T07` bake in as defaults.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Run the E08 ingestion path (modules M3-M6) writing to QuestDB through the E07 tier wiring for **BTCUSDT** and **ETHUSDT** for **7 consecutive days**, at `orderbook_depth` 50 and 200.
- Measure the on-disk delta per QuestDB table: `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `liquidations` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4).
- Measure the Parquet size of the same window after a manual roll-off, giving the hot->cold compression ratio.
- Publish `docs/plan/notes/e16-storage-measurement.md`: GB/day per (symbol, stream, depth), hot/cold ratio, peak-hour vs quiet-hour ratio, recommended `CV_DISK_CAP_GB`, `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS`, `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- PR updating budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the Validation section of `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md` with the measured range.

## Out of scope
- Any production code in M10/M11 - the spike uses throwaway scripts under `scripts/spikes/e16-storage/`.
- Symbols beyond BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT and any non-USDT-perp instrument.
- Tuning QuestDB partitioning/compression - a finding of this spike, not a deliverable.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Measured figures replace the estimate
  Given 7 days of continuous capture for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  When the measurement note is published
  Then it states GB/day per stream per symbol at depth 50 and depth 200 with the observation window and the gap minutes excluded
  And budget #12 in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md is updated with the measured range

Scenario: Capture was not continuous
  Given the capture run contains a gap longer than 10 minutes
  When GB/day is computed
  Then the gap duration is subtracted from the denominator and the note records the gap explicitly rather than reporting a diluted rate

Scenario: Measurement contradicts the estimate by more than 2x
  Given the measured depth-200 rate for BTCUSDT exceeds 1.5 GB/day
  Then the spike raises a follow-up against E16-T06 and E16-T07 to revise retention defaults before those tickets close
  And the Architect is tagged for a decision on the hot-tier window
```

## Context
M10 Recorder needs its relational state before any recorder code can run. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6 specifies the four tables verbatim; this task lands them as a migration plus models and a repository. - Alembic migration `0007_recorder` under `services/api/migrations/versions/`, creating exactly what `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6 specifies:

  - `recording_sessions` with `recs_counts`, `recs_window`, indexes `ix_recs_symbol_time`, `ix_recs_live`.
  - `recording_gaps` with `rg_window`, `rg_cause`, index `ix_rg_symbol_time`.
  - `retention_policies` with `rp_scope`, `rp_symshape`, `rp_days`, `rp_downshape`, `rp_disk`, indexes `ux_rp_default`, `ux_rp_symbol`.
- Seed one `scope='default'` `retention_policies` row per stream from the retention matrix in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §7 (trades 30 d, orderbook_delta 7 d, orderbook_snapshots 30 d, tickers 30 d, klines 90 d, liquidations 90 d, heatmap_cells 7 d, ...), `action='archive_parquet'` except `engine_metrics` -> `drop`.
- SQLAlchemy models plus `RecorderRepository`: `list_recorded(env)`, `get_by_symbol(symbol, env)`, `upsert_auto(symbol, reason, ref)`, `soft_remove(id)`, `open_session(...)`, `close_session(id, reason)`, `record_gap(...)`, `resolve_policy(symbol, stream)`.
- Working downgrade dropping tables and enums.

## Out of scope
- QuestDB table DDL (E07) and Parquet layout (E16-T05).
- REST/WS surfaces (E16-T08).
- Retention execution (E16-T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and rolls back cleanly
  Given a database at revision 0006
  When alembic upgrade head, downgrade -1 and upgrade head are run in sequence
  Then all four tables and three enums exist with the specified constraints and no error is raised

Scenario: Duplicate active recording is impossible
  Given an active recorded_symbols row for (BTCUSDT, live) with removed_at NULL
  When a second active row for the same pair is inserted
  Then the insert fails on ux_rs_symbol
  And the same insert succeeds after the first row is soft-removed

Scenario: Policy resolution is most-specific-first
  Given a default trades policy of 30 days and a symbol policy for (ETHUSDT, trades) of 3 days
  When resolve_policy is called for ETHUSDT/trades it returns 3
  And for BTCUSDT/trades it returns 30

Scenario: Pinned symbol overrides every policy
  Given BTCUSDT has pinned = true
  When resolve_policy is called for any stream of BTCUSDT
  Then it returns the infinite-retention sentinel regardless of the symbol or default policy

Scenario: Degenerate gap is rejected
  When a recording_gaps row with gap_end <= gap_start is inserted
  Then the rg_window constraint rejects it
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolution order (§3.6.3): pinned symbol -> infinite (`retain_days=None` sentinel); else symbol-scoped policy; else default policy; else hard default 30 days. Implement as one statement with `ORDER BY (scope='symbol') DESC LIMIT 1`.
- `reason_refs` is jsonb `[{"kind":"chart","id":"..."},{"kind":"position","id":"..."}]`; expose `add_reason_ref`/`remove_reason_ref` as single-statement jsonb updates to avoid a read-modify-write race against the auto-record path in E16-T02.
- `removed_at` is a soft delete - nothing in E16 hard-deletes a `recorded_symbols` row, so historical sessions stay attributable.
- Postgres has no `CREATE TYPE IF NOT EXISTS`; guard enum creation with a DO block on `pg_type`.

## Test plan
- Unit (testcontainers Postgres): one test per constraint above, each asserting the constraint name in the raised error; repository method tests for each public method.
- Migration round-trip `upgrade->downgrade->upgrade` in CI.
- Seed test: `count(*) FROM retention_policies WHERE scope='default'` equals the number of §7 rows mapping to a `stream_kind`.
- Coverage target >=85% on `recorder/repository.py`.

## Security notes
`recorded_symbols.added_by` is the audit anchor for who started recording. Classification **internal** (no PII, no secrets). Grants: API role gets SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE; **no role gets DELETE** on `recording_sessions` or `recording_gaps` - deleting gap metadata would hide a gap, which ADR-0015 §7 forbids ("no interpolation, ever"). No `security` review label needed.

N/A - no UI.

`ix_recs_live` is partial so the per-second "what is recording now" query behind the `recorder` WS topic stays an index-only scan; assert the plan with `EXPLAIN` in a test.

Log migration start/finish with revision ids at INFO. No new metrics.

ADR-0015 decision 1 defines the effective recorded set as *explicit user list union symbols with an open chart union symbols with an open position*. `RecordingPolicy` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) is the single component that owns this union and the transitions in and out of it. It implements US-REC-001 (manual list, empty by default) and US-REC-002 (auto-record triggers with a grace period), and it is the gate every other recorder component asks "should I be capturing this symbol right now".

Getting the grace periods right is a product requirement, not an optimisation: ADR-0015 consequences call out that auto-recording on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols, mitigated by a 60 s open-before-start delay; US-REC-002 requires a configurable stop grace period defaulting to 30 min so a briefly closed chart does not fragment a session into gaps.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/policy.py` - `RecordingPolicy` with `effective_set() -> dict[symbol, EffectiveEntry]`, `on_chart_opened/closed(symbol, chart_id)`, `on_position_opened/closed(symbol, position_id)`, `add_manual(symbol, user_id, streams, depth)`, `remove_manual(symbol)`, `set_pin(symbol, pinned)`.

```gherkin
  Given CV_RECORDER_AUTOSTART_DELAY_S is 60
  When a chart for SOLUSDT is opened and closed after 20 seconds

```

title: Implement StreamWriter: batched QuestDB writes, WAL spill and recovery
body:
## Context
`StreamWriter` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) is the hot path that turns normalised exchange events into durable rows. ADR-0015 decision 2 makes the raw streams the source of truth - derived series are recomputable, so losing a tick is permanent while losing a footprint cell is not. Decision 8 requires a bounded on-disk WAL spill when QuestDB is unavailable, replayed on recovery, so a database restart costs latency rather than history.

The specific failure this component exists to prevent is silent loss: dropping messages under backpressure without recording a gap would leave a hole that later looks like a quiet market (US-REC-006, "I never mistake a gap for calm").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/writer.py` - `StreamWriter` consuming normalised events from M4/M5/M6 for symbols in the effective set, writing to QuestDB via ILP: tables `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `liquidations` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4).
- Batching: flush on 10 000 rows **or** 200 ms, whichever first (§3.8); per-stream batches so a slow stream never delays another.
- Backpressure ladder: in-memory queue -> bounded on-disk WAL (`CV_RECORDER_WAL_MAX_BYTES`, default 1 GiB, under `CV_RECORDER_WAL_DIR`) -> drop with an explicit `recording_gaps` row (`cause='backpressure_drop'`) and a critical event. Never drop silently.
- WAL replay on startup and on QuestDB recovery, in `exch_ts` order, idempotent (duplicate suppression by `(symbol, stream, exch_ts, seq)`).
- Per-symbol counters written back to `recording_sessions` (`messages_received`, `messages_dropped`, `bytes_written`, `reconnect_count`) every 10 s.
- Metrics `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `recorder_write_backlog_rows`, `recorder_flush_duration_seconds`.

## Out of scope
- Session and gap lifecycle from WS disconnects (E16-T04) - this task only records gaps caused by its own backpressure drops.
- Roll-off to Parquet (E16-T05) and retention (E16-T06).
- Derived series (bars, footprint, heatmap) - owned by E12/E18/E21; StreamWriter writes raw streams only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Steady-state write path
  Given BTCUSDT is recording at depth 200
  When 10 minutes of live tape and book deltas are ingested
  Then every event appears exactly once in the corresponding QuestDB table
  And recorder_write_backlog_rows stays at 0 at p95

Scenario: QuestDB unavailable spills rather than drops
  Given QuestDB is stopped
  When 2 minutes of events arrive
  Then events are appended to the on-disk WAL, recorder_spill_bytes rises and no rows are dropped
  And when QuestDB returns, the WAL is replayed in exch_ts order and the WAL file is truncated

Scenario: WAL exhaustion is recorded as an explicit gap
  Given the WAL has reached CV_RECORDER_WAL_MAX_BYTES and QuestDB is still unavailable
  When further events arrive
  Then they are dropped, a recording_gaps row with cause "backpressure_drop" covering the dropped window is written
  And a critical system event naming the symbol is raised

Scenario: Replay is idempotent
  Given a WAL replay is interrupted halfway and restarted
  When the replay completes
  Then no duplicate rows exist for any (symbol, stream, exch_ts, seq)

Scenario: One slow stream does not stall the others
  Given orderbook_deltas writes are artificially delayed by 2 seconds
  Then trades continue to flush on their own 200 ms cadence
```

## Technical notes / design
- ILP over TCP with the QuestDB client's auto-flush disabled; the writer owns the cadence so flush timing is testable.
- Duplicate suppression on replay uses QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` where the table declares them, and a bloom-filtered in-process set for the current replay batch otherwise.
- WAL format: length-prefixed msgpack frames `{stream, symbol, exch_ts, seq, payload}` with a 4-byte CRC per frame; a frame failing CRC ends the replay at that point and the remainder is quarantined to `<wal>/corrupt/` with a gap recorded - never silently skipped mid-file.
- Sequence handling: a `seq` jump on `orderbook_deltas` is **not** StreamWriter's problem to heal (E08 resubscribes and resnapshots); StreamWriter records the observed jump so E16-T04 can convert it to a `seq_jump` gap.
- Error codes: `recorder_write_failed`, `recorder_wal_full`, `recorder_wal_corrupt`.

## Test plan
- Unit: batching boundaries (exactly 10 000 rows, exactly 200 ms), WAL frame round-trip, CRC failure handling, dedup on replay.
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB): the five acceptance scenarios, including a real container stop/start for the spill case.
- Chaos: kill -9 the process mid-flush; assert on restart that the WAL replays and the resulting row count equals produced minus dropped, with a gap row for the difference (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` chaos suite, SR-154).
- Perf: sustain 50 000 events/s for 10 minutes with p95 flush < 50 ms and backlog 0; recorded as a benchmark in CI trend.
- Coverage >=85% on `recorder/writer.py`.

## Security notes
Threat S2 (disk DoS, **Critical**, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8): the WAL is bounded and lives on the recording volume, which SR-096 requires to be separate from the volume the backend and Postgres need - assert the mount differs at startup and refuse to start recording if it does not. Raw exchange payloads retained for forensics are kept 7 days only (ADR-0015 decision 5) and are redacted of any account-scoped field before storage. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budget: ingest 50k msg/s sustained, p95 flush < 50 ms, memory ceiling 512 MiB for queues (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`). Measured GB/day must match the E16-K01 figures within 20%; a larger divergence is a bug in batching or depth configuration.

## Observability
The metrics listed in Scope, plus alert rules: `recorder_spill_bytes > 0` for 5 min -> warning; any `recorder_rows_dropped_total` increase -> critical page.

title: Implement RollOffJob: verified hot-to-cold Parquet export and weekly compaction
body:
## Context
US-REC-004 requires recent data in the hot tier and older data archived so queries stay fast and storage stays affordable, with the hard rule that hot data is dropped **only after a verified write**. ADR-0015 decision 3 sets the hot window at `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (default 7) with a nightly export to Parquet. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5-§6 defines the Parquet layout, the DuckDB views over it and the weekly compactor that merges the small files the nightly export produces.

The failure mode this guards against is the worst one available to a recorder: dropping a hot partition after a corrupt or partial archive write, destroying irreplaceable data (Bybit has no historical L2 to re-fetch).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/rolloff.py` - nightly job exporting QuestDB partitions older than the per-stream hot window (`retention_policies.retain_days` for the hot tier) to Parquet under the layout in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5, then dropping the hot partition **only** after verification.
- Verification: row count match **and** checksum match between source partition and written Parquet file (US-REC-004 NFR). Mismatch -> hot data retained, `archive.verification_failed` alert raised, job retries with exponential backoff and does not advance the watermark.
- Roll-off watermark per `(symbol, stream)` persisted so `CoverageService` (E16-T04) can attribute tiers.
- DuckDB view registration so a query spanning both tiers is served seamlessly, with the tiers used reported in the query detail (`meta.sources` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` responses).
- Weekly compactor merging small Parquet files into target-sized partitions (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5.4), exposed as `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/compact` (async, job id polled via `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`).
- Cold-cold rollup: partitions older than 180 days for `orderbook_deltas` and `heatmap_cells` are downsampled to 1 s book snapshots per `retention_policies.action='downsample'` rather than merged.

## Out of scope
- Deleting cold data at the retention horizon (E16-T06).
- Disk-pressure acceleration (E16-T07).
- Backups and restore (`/admin/backups/*` - platform/ops epic).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Nightly roll-off archives then drops
  Given trades partitions older than the hot window exist for BTCUSDT
  When the nightly roll-off runs
  Then Parquet files are written under the documented layout, row counts and checksums match, the hot partition is dropped and the watermark advances

Scenario: Verification failure never loses data
  Given the Parquet write produces a file whose row count differs from the source partition
  When verification runs
  Then the hot partition is NOT dropped, the partial Parquet file is quarantined, an alert is raised and the job retries with backoff

Scenario: Cross-tier query is seamless
  Given trades for a symbol span Parquet and QuestDB
  When a 14-day window is queried
  Then one merged, correctly ordered result is returned and meta.sources lists both questdb and parquet

Scenario: Compaction is safe under concurrent reads
  Given a replay session is reading a cold partition
  When compaction targets that partition
  Then compaction defers it, logs the deferral and completes the remaining partitions

Scenario: Downsample past 180 days
  Given orderbook_deltas partitions older than 180 days
  When the rollup runs
  Then they are replaced by 1 second book snapshots and the coverage report labels the range as downsampled
```

## Technical notes / design
- Export unit is one (symbol, stream, day) partition, processed newest-first so an interrupted run leaves the oldest data in the hot tier rather than a half-migrated middle.
- Checksum: SHA-256 over the canonical column-ordered Arrow batches, computed on read-back of the written file (not on the in-memory buffer) - a verification that never re-reads the file does not verify anything.
- Quarantine path `<parquet_root>/_quarantine/<stream>/<symbol>/<date>/` with the failure reason in a sidecar JSON; quarantined files are never registered in DuckDB views.
- Concurrency: the job takes a Postgres advisory lock per `(symbol, stream)`; the replay engine takes a shared read lease on ranges it is using, which the compactor honours (US-REC-003 NFR: never delete or rewrite data currently being read by a replay or backtest).
- Config: `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_PARQUET_ROOT`, `CV_COMPACT_TARGET_MB` (default 256), `CV_ROLLOFF_CRON` (default `0 3 * * *`).
- Error codes: `archive_verification_failed`, `archive_write_failed`, `compaction_deferred`.

## Test plan
- Unit: watermark advance/rollback, checksum computation, quarantine on mismatch, newest-first ordering, advisory-lock contention.
- Integration (QuestDB + local Parquet): full export-verify-drop cycle on a seeded day; injected mismatch asserting no drop; cross-tier query correctness against a known row set.
- Chaos: kill the job between write and verify, and between verify and drop; assert no data loss in either case and that a re-run converges.
- Perf: export of one day of depth-200 `orderbook_deltas` (the largest stream) completes within the nightly window and uses < 2 GiB RSS.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Path traversal in `archive_path` / `CV_PARQUET_ROOT` is an explicit epic-level threat (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` security row for E16): every path is resolved and asserted to be inside the configured root before any write or delete; symlinks are rejected. Deletion of a hot partition is audited with symbol, stream, range and row count (`retention_purge`-class audit entry). Requires the `security` review label on the PR.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. Job progress surfaces through SCR-142 (E16-S04).

## Performance notes
The job must not degrade live ingestion: throttle to `CV_ROLLOFF_MAX_MBPS` (default 200) and yield between partitions; assert ingest p95 lag is unchanged during a roll-off in the integration test.

## Observability
Metrics `recorder_rolloff_bytes_total{stream}`, `recorder_rolloff_duration_seconds`, `recorder_rolloff_failures_total{reason}`, `recorder_watermark_lag_days{symbol,stream}`. Alert when watermark lag exceeds hot window + 2 days.

- [ ] Coverage >=85%.

- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner and a DevSecOps review.

title: Implement RetentionManager: policy resolution, dry-run preview, reaper and purge
body:
## Context
US-REC-003 is the ticket where data is irreversibly destroyed, so it is the ticket with the least room for error. The owner decision is a 30-day default with per-symbol overrides and `pinned = true` meaning never delete (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §6). The story requires a **dry run** that reports exactly what would be deleted by symbol, range and size before anything is removed, and an NFR that pruning is off-peak, resumable, and never deletes data currently being read by a replay or backtest.

ADR-0015 decision 9 adds that deletion is auditable and the audit entry outlives the data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/retention.py` - `RetentionManager` with `resolve(symbol, stream) -> EffectivePolicy`, `preview(scope) -> PrunePlan`, `run(plan, dry_run: bool)`.
- Resolution order (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6.3): pinned symbol -> infinite; else symbol-scoped policy; else default policy; else hard default 30 days. `applies_to_pinned: true` on a policy is the only way to touch pinned data, and it requires step-up.
- Nightly reaper: drops QuestDB partitions past the hot horizon (already archived by E16-T05) and deletes Parquet partition directories past the total horizon, per the matrix in §7. Resumable: progress checkpointed per `(symbol, stream, partition)` so an interrupted run resumes rather than restarts.
- Read-lease honouring: a partition covered by an active replay/backtest lease is skipped and retried on the next pass, never deleted mid-read.
- `PrunePlan`: per symbol, stream, date range, estimated bytes and row count, total bytes freed, and an explicit list of what is protected and why (pinned / leased / inside hot window).
- Irreversible purge (`POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge`): requires an elevated session, a mandatory `reason` (3-280 chars) and a `confirm_symbol` echo equal to `symbol`; refuses pinned symbols unless `include_pinned` is set; always audited with the exact window deleted; asynchronous with a job id.
- Audit events `retention.run`, `retention.change`, `data.deleted`, `retention.purge` carrying symbol, stream, range, row count and actor; retained after the data is gone.

## Out of scope
- Disk-pressure accelerated mode (E16-T07).
- The retention editor UI (E16-S03) and the REST policy endpoints (E16-T08).
- Postgres-side retention for OMS/journal tables (owned by their epics).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default retention prunes on schedule
  Given the default trades retention is 30 days and BTCUSDT is not pinned
  When the nightly reaper runs
  Then trades partitions older than 30 days are deleted, the freed bytes are reported and the next prune time is recorded

Scenario: Pinned data is never deleted
  Given ETHUSDT is pinned and has data older than every configured horizon
  When the reaper runs with any policy that does not set applies_to_pinned
  Then nothing for ETHUSDT is deleted and the plan lists it as protected with reason "pinned"

Scenario: Dry run deletes nothing
  When a prune preview is requested
  Then it reports exactly what would be deleted by symbol, range and size
  And a byte-for-byte comparison of the data volume before and after shows no change

Scenario: Data under active replay is not deleted
  Given a replay session holds a lease on a partition eligible for deletion
  When the reaper reaches that partition
  Then it is skipped with reason "leased", logged, and retried on the next pass

Scenario: Interrupted run resumes
  Given the reaper is killed after processing 3 of 10 symbols
  When it next runs
  Then it resumes from the checkpoint and does not re-scan the completed symbols

Scenario: Purge requires an exact confirmation
  Given an owner requests a purge of BTCUSDT with confirm_symbol "BTCUSD"
  Then the request is rejected 422 and nothing is deleted
  And with the correct echo, an elevated session and a reason, the purge is accepted, executed and audited with the exact window

Scenario: Shortening retention warns with the real number
  Given trades retention is reduced from 30 to 7 days
  When the change is previewed
  Then the plan states the exact GB and date range that become eligible for deletion before the change is applied
```

## Technical notes / design
- Deletion primitives: QuestDB `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION WHERE ts < dateadd('d', -N, now())` (§6); Parquet deletion is a directory unlink after the DuckDB view is de-registered, with the path containment check from E16-T05 applied again at the delete site.
- The reaper's **first** predicate is the pin check, exactly as §6 specifies: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM recorded_symbols WHERE symbol = $1 AND pinned AND removed_at IS NULL)`.
- Un-pinning does not retroactively delete: the next pass applies the normal policy, and the API returns the exact volume that will be dropped so the UI (E16-S03) can warn.
- Ordering guarantee: raw-tick retention must be >= the retention of anything derived from it within the same stream family; the policy validator rejects a set where `bars_*` outlive `trades` (the SCR-141 validation rule "bars can't be deleted before the ticks they came from").
- Off-peak: default cron `0 4 * * *`, configurable via `CV_RETENTION_CRON`; the run yields if ingest lag rises above 1 s.
- Error codes: `retention_invalid_policy`, `retention_pinned_refused`, `purge_confirmation_mismatch`, `purge_requires_elevation`.

## Test plan
- Unit: resolution matrix (pinned/symbol/default/hard-default x 5 streams), validator rejecting inverted tick/bar retention, checkpoint resume, plan arithmetic.
- Integration: seeded multi-symbol dataset run through preview then real run, asserting exact byte and row deltas; pinned-symbol immunity; lease skip; purge happy path and all three refusal paths.
- Chaos: kill the reaper mid-partition; assert no partially deleted partition is left registered in DuckDB and that a re-run converges.
- Security test: purge without elevation -> 403; with mismatched echo -> 422; against a pinned symbol without `include_pinned` -> 422.
- Coverage >=90% on `recorder/retention.py` (destructive code path, above the standard bar).

## Security notes
This is the highest-severity code in the epic: an authorization or predicate bug destroys irreplaceable data. Controls: `recording:write` plus step-up for purge (permission 51 in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §13); mandatory reason; typed confirmation; pin check first; audit before delete and after delete (both, so a crash between them is detectable); path containment. Threat coverage: tampering (policy change to destroy data), repudiation (audit), DoS (mass purge). **PR requires the `security` label and Security-engineer sign-off.** Classification **internal**, but deletion is irreversible so treated as a high-impact action.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI in this ticket; consequences are surfaced by SCR-141 (E16-S03).

## Performance notes
A full reaper pass over 20 symbols x 10 streams completes in < 10 minutes and never raises ingest p95 lag above the live budget; partition drops are metadata operations, so wall time is dominated by Parquet unlinks, which are batched.

title: Implement DiskBudget: measured growth, projection and the disk-pressure ladder
body:
## Context
Unbounded recording filling the disk and taking the trading host down is rated **Critical** (threat S2, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8, control SR-096). US-REC-005 requires measured - not estimated - per-symbol GB/day, a projection of days of runway, a warning when the budget would be exceeded within 7 days, and a hard limit at which new recording is suspended while existing data is preserved.

ADR-0015 decision 6 fixes the ladder: alert at 80% of `CV_DISK_CAP_GB`, auto-recording stops accepting new symbols at 90% (explicit-list symbols keep recording), recording halts entirely at 95% with a critical alert. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §6 adds the free-space ladder: below 15% free the reaper accelerates; below 5% free, ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols pauses. Pinned data is never deleted automatically - the system stops recording rather than discarding what the user asked to keep.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/budget.py` - `DiskBudget` sampling volume usage and per-symbol/per-tier sizes **every 60 s** (SCR-142 requires server-side sampling, never on-request computation), persisting a rolling series for growth-rate calculation.
- Measured daily growth per symbol from the sampled series (7-day linear fit, falling back to 24 h when less data exists), projected `disk_full_at`, and days-of-runway - the fields behind `GET /api/v1/recording/storage`.
- Ladder implementation with hysteresis (re-arm 5 percentage points below each trigger):
  - 75-80%: warning system event with concrete suggested actions (reduce depth tier, shorten retention, unpin).
  - 90% of cap **or** <15% free: refuse new auto-record entries; accelerate the reaper (halve effective retention for non-pinned symbols in ascending `recorded_symbols.priority` until free space exceeds 25%).
  - 95% of cap **or** <5% free: pause ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols, then halt recording entirely; raise a critical event; existing data preserved.
- Volume separation assertion at startup (SR-096): the recording volume must differ from the volume Postgres and the backend need; if it does not, log a critical warning and refuse to enable recording unless `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME=true`.
- Trading-path independence: recording suspension must never disable order placement - asserted by test, stated in the UI copy for SCR-142.

## Out of scope
- The UI for budget display (E16-S01, E16-S04) and the alert delivery channel (E40).
- Retention execution itself (E16-T06); this task only signals accelerated mode.
- Backup sizing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Figures are measured, not estimated
  Given 7 days of 60-second usage samples for BTCUSDT
  When storage usage is requested
  Then daily_growth_bytes is derived from the sampled series and is within 20 percent of the measured GB/day figure from the E16-K01 note

Scenario: Budget warning fires before the wall
  Given the projection shows the configured cap will be exceeded in 6 days
  Then a warning event fires naming the projected date and listing reduce-depth, shorten-retention and unpin as actions

Scenario: Auto-record stops but the explicit list keeps recording
  Given usage reaches 90 percent of CV_DISK_CAP_GB
  When a chart is opened for an unrecorded symbol
  Then auto-record is refused with a warning event
  And symbols on the explicit manual list continue recording uninterrupted

Scenario: Hard limit preserves data and trading
  Given usage reaches 95 percent
  Then recording halts, a critical alert fires, no recorded data is deleted, and placing an order still succeeds

Scenario: Pinned data survives disk pressure
  Given free space falls below 5 percent and a pinned symbol holds most of the data
  Then the pinned data is not deleted, ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, and the critical event names the pinned symbol as the dominant consumer

Scenario: Hysteresis prevents flapping
  Given usage oscillates between 89 and 91 percent
  Then the auto-record refusal engages once and does not re-arm until usage falls below 85 percent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sampling uses `statvfs` for the volume and QuestDB `tables()` / Parquet directory sizes for per-tier and per-symbol attribution; per-symbol attribution for Parquet comes from the partition path, so it is exact rather than apportioned.
- Growth fit ignores samples inside recorded gaps so an outage does not depress the projected rate.
- Ladder decisions are published as `DiskPressureChanged` events consumed by `RecordingPolicy` (E16-T02) and `RetentionManager` (E16-T06); the budget component never deletes anything itself, which keeps deletion authority in exactly one place.
- Config: `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` (500, revised by E16-K01), `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT` (80), `CV_DISK_AUTOSTOP_PCT` (90), `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` (95), `CV_DISK_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_S` (60), `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` (false).

## Test plan
- Unit: projection maths with gaps, hysteresis state machine, ladder thresholds by both cap-percentage and free-space paths.
- Integration: a loopback volume filled to 76%, 81%, 91% and 96% asserting each documented behaviour including pinned survival and trading availability (the disk-pressure chaos test named in ADR-0015 Validation and SR-154).
- Contract: `StorageUsage` response validated against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Directly implements SR-096 and mitigates the Critical DoS S2. Additional checks: the sampler must not shell out (no `du` subprocess with user-controlled paths); volume separation asserted at startup; the suggested-actions text must not leak absolute host paths to non-owner roles. **PR carries the `security` label.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI here; the meter and its numeric text are specified in E16-D02/E16-D04 and built in E16-S01/E16-S04.

## Performance notes
Sampling costs < 50 ms per pass and never blocks ingestion; the 60 s cadence is a budget, not a target to beat.

## Observability
Metrics `disk_used_ratio`, `disk_free_bytes`, `recorder_disk_pressure_level`, `recorder_bytes_per_day{symbol}`, `recorder_projected_full_timestamp`. Alerts: warning at `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT`, critical at `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT`, and a page if `recorder_disk_pressure_level > 0` for over 24 h.

- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` default updated from the E16-K01 measurement.
- [ ] Security sign-off on SR-096 compliance.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner and DevSecOps.

`E16-T03` supplies the write-rate signal; `E16-K01` supplies the measured constants this ladder is sized against.

body:
## Context
The recorder is useless without the contract the web app talks to. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies every path under the `recording` tag and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.8 specifies the `RecorderUpdate` frame at a 1000 ms cadence. This task implements exactly that contract - interface-first, so the frontend stories (E16-S01..S05) can be built against a green contract test rather than a guess.

## Scope / Deliverables
- REST handlers implementing, byte-for-byte against the existing OpenAPI spec:
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` (`listRecordedSymbols`), `POST /api/v1/recording/symbols`
  - `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}` (PATCH covers pin, retention, depth; DELETE stops recording and retains data; `?purge_data=true` is deprecated and answers 422 `validation_failed` (`use_purge_route`), so `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge` is the one destructive path)
  - `POST /api/v1/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}/pin`
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/status` (`getRecordingStatus`)
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` (`getStorageUsage`)
  - `GET|PUT /api/v1/recording/retention-policies` (`?apply_now=true` triggers an immediate sweep)
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/sessions` (cursor-paginated)
  - `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage` (`getDataCoverage`)
  - `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/compact`, `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge` (both async, returning `job_id`)
- RBAC per the spec `x-rbac` blocks: `recording:read` for reads, `recording:write` for writes, step-up elevation for purge (permission 51, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §13).
- Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` required on compact and purge, optional on the retention PUT.
- WS topic `recorder` (param `symbols`, cadence 1000 ms, permission `recording:read`, scope none) publishing `RecorderUpdate` exactly per §15.8: `overall`, `connections[]`, `symbols[]` (with `state`, `reason`, `pinned`, `lag_ms`, `rows_last_hour`, `dropped_messages`, `resyncs_last_hour`, `disk_bytes`, `last_event_at_ms`), `ingest_rate_msgs_per_sec`, `write_backlog_rows`, `storage`.

- Generated TypeScript client types regenerated in `packages/api-client` from the OpenAPI spec.

```gherkin
  When the contract suite runs every recording path against docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then every request and response validates, including the documented examples

Scenario: Empty by default
  Given a fresh installation
  When GET /api/v1/recording/symbols is called
  Then it returns an empty list with a 200, not a 404

Scenario: Stop retains data
  When DELETE /api/v1/recording/symbols/{id} is called without purge_data
  Then it answers 204, and within 5 seconds the row shows lingering: true with linger_until
  And recording stops and the session is closed when the grace window ends (E16-D02 §6.2)
  And the recorded data remains queryable, and the stop dialog states that retention policy now governs it

Scenario: Purge needs elevation and an exact echo
  Given an owner session without step-up elevation
  When POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge is called
  Then 403 is returned and nothing is deleted
  And with elevation but confirm_symbol not equal to symbol, 422 purge_confirmation_mismatch is returned

Scenario: Viewer cannot write
  Given a Viewer session
  When POST /api/v1/recording/symbols is called
  Then 403 is returned and the attempt is audited

Scenario: WS recorder topic streams at 1 Hz
  Given a client subscribes to the recorder topic for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  Then a snapshot frame arrives first, followed by updates at approximately 1000 ms
  And every frame validates against the RecorderUpdate schema

Scenario: Historical request before recording start is refused honestly
  Given recording for SOLUSDT started yesterday
  When bars are requested for a window entirely before that
  Then 422 no_data_recorded is returned carrying recording_started_at
```

> **Deviation (coordinator ruling, 2026-10-23 09:45Z, Q1–Q3):** AC3 is amended. The signed-off E16-D02 §6.2 keeps recording through a grace window after a stop, so "stops within 5 seconds" became the `lingering` row within 5 s, with the stop at the grace end. The response stays `204`, and the retention statement is the stop dialog's copy. `?purge_data=true` is deprecated in favour of the purge route. The JSON twin is amended in the contract PR (S0).

## Technical notes / design
- Handlers are thin: all logic lives in the M10 services from T02/T04/T06/T07. The route layer only maps DTOs, enforces RBAC via `ScopeResolver` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10) and applies idempotency.
- `GET /recording/status` and the WS topic share one cached `RecordingStatus` snapshot refreshed at 1 Hz, so N subscribers cost one computation.
- `PUT /recording/retention-policies` replaces the whole set atomically in one transaction, validated by the E16-T06 policy validator before commit; `apply_now=true` enqueues a sweep rather than running it inline.
- Storage figures are served from the 60 s sample (E16-T07), never computed per request.
- Audit: `recorder.start`, `recorder.stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`, `storage.compaction_triggered` with actor, before/after and the affected window.

- Contract: schemathesis/openapi-core against every path and the documented examples; WS frames validated against the JSON Schema in §15.8.

## Context
US-REC-008's NFR states the specific failure this whole epic guards against: "silently stopped" recording. A recorder that stops without anyone noticing produces exactly the outcome ADR-0015 was written to prevent - a hole in history discovered months later when a profile or replay needs it. Metrics existing is not the same as someone being told; this task turns the metrics from T02/T03/T04/T06/T07 into dashboards, alert rules and a runbook.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Grafana dashboard `recorder` (provisioned as code in `ops/grafana/dashboards/recorder.json`): per-symbol ingest rate, lag, rows/hour, dropped messages, write backlog, spill bytes, disk used ratio with the 80/90/95 thresholds drawn, projected full date, gap count by cause, retention last-success age, roll-off watermark lag.
- Prometheus alert rules in `ops/prometheus/rules/recorder.yml`:
  - `RecorderSilentStop` - a symbol in state `recording` with zero writes for 60 s while the market is active -> **critical**, names the symbol (US-REC-008 scenario 3).
  - `RecorderMessagesDropped` - any increase in `recorder_rows_dropped_total` -> critical.
  - `RecorderSpilling` - `recorder_spill_bytes > 0` for 5 min -> warning.
  - `DiskWarn` / `DiskCritical` at `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT` / `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` -> warning / critical.
  - `RetentionStale` - `retention_last_success_timestamp` older than 48 h -> warning.
  - `RollOffWatermarkLag` - watermark lag > hot window + 2 days -> warning.
  - `RecorderGapBurst` - more than 5 gaps in an hour for one symbol -> warning.
- Runbook `docs/ops/runbooks/recorder.md`: one section per alert with symptom, first three checks, remediation, and what NOT to do (never delete gap rows; never clear the WAL without recording a gap).
- "Market active" definition for the silent-stop rule: the shared public WS connection has received any message for any symbol in the last 10 s - so a venue-wide outage pages once, not per symbol.

## Out of scope
- Notification delivery channels (E40 alerts epic) - these rules fire into the existing E04 observability baseline.
- Application metric instrumentation itself (shipped by T02/T03/T04/T06/T07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Silent stop pages within 90 seconds
  Given BTCUSDT is in state recording and its writer is suspended while other symbols keep writing
  When 60 seconds pass
  Then RecorderSilentStop fires as critical and the alert annotation names BTCUSDT

Scenario: Venue outage does not fan out
  Given the public WS connection receives nothing for any symbol
  When the silent-stop rule is evaluated
  Then it does not fire per symbol; the connection-level alert fires once

Scenario: Every alert has a runbook
  When the alert rules file is linted
  Then every rule has a runbook_url annotation resolving to a section that exists in docs/ops/runbooks/recorder.md

Scenario: Dashboard provisions from code
  Given a clean Grafana instance
  When provisioning runs
  Then the recorder dashboard appears with every listed panel populated from live metrics
```

## Technical notes / design
- Alert rules are unit-tested with `promtool test rules` using recorded metric series fixtures - an alert rule with no test is an alert rule that fires at 3 a.m. for the wrong reason.
- Thresholds are templated from the same config keys the application uses so a change to `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` does not silently desynchronise the alert from the behaviour.
- Dashboard panels use the exact metric names shipped by T03/T07 (`recorder_rows_total`, `recorder_bytes_written_total`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `disk_used_ratio`, `recorder_gaps_total`, `retention_last_success_timestamp`, `recorder_watermark_lag_days`).

## Test plan
- `promtool test rules` fixtures for each of the seven rules, including the venue-outage negative case.
- Provisioning smoke test in CI: spin Grafana, provision, assert the dashboard exists and every panel query parses.
- Manual: trigger a real silent stop in the staging environment and record the time to alert in the ticket.

## Security notes
Dashboards must not expose host absolute paths or symbol-level data to unauthenticated viewers; Grafana sits behind the same Tailscale-only boundary as the app. Alert annotations must not embed credentials or full file paths. SR-125 requires the disk high-watermark metric to be exported and alerted on - this ticket is its implementation for E16.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - operational dashboards, not product UI. Panel titles still carry units so figures are unambiguous.

## Performance notes
Scrape interval 15 s; the recorder job adds fewer than 200 series per symbol; cardinality is bounded by `CV_RECORDER_MAX_SYMBOLS`.

## Observability
This ticket *is* observability. It additionally adds a synthetic `recorder_up` gauge so absence of the exporter itself is alertable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Dashboard and rules merged as code and provisioned in staging.
- [ ] `promtool` rule tests green in CI.
- [ ] Runbook sections exist for all seven alerts and are linked from each rule.
- [ ] Time-to-alert for a real induced silent stop recorded in the ticket.
- [ ] 1 DevSecOps approval plus backend code-owner.

## Dependencies

title: Implement resumable bulk import of Bybit public trade archives
body:
## Context
US-REC-007 (Should) lets the owner import Bybit's public historical trade archives so there is *some* depth before the recorder existed. It is explicitly partial relief: the archives carry trades only - no book data, no liquidations - so imported ranges must be labelled archive-derived and must never let a profile or footprint pretend it has book-quality history for that window.

The rule that keeps the data honest is recorded-wins: where an import overlaps data the recorder captured, the recorded data is authoritative and the overlap is reported rather than merged.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/importer.py` - downloads a date range of Bybit public trade archives for a symbol, validates checksums, converts to the canonical `trades` schema and writes directly to the cold Parquet tier under the E16-T05 layout.
- Resumability: per-file checkpoint so an interrupted import resumes at the next unprocessed file; re-running a completed import is a no-op.
- Rate limiting on downloads (`CV_IMPORT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, default 2; `CV_IMPORT_MAX_MBPS`, default 50) so an import never starves live ingestion.
- Overlap handling: for any window already covered by `recording_sessions`, recorded data wins; imported rows in that window are discarded, counted and reported in the summary. No duplicates are created.
- Labelling: imported intervals are registered in coverage as `source='archive'` with `streams=['trades']` only, so `CoverageService` (E16-T04) reports book-level coverage for those windows as absent.
- Corrupt-file handling: a file failing checksum or parsing is skipped, recorded in the summary with its name and the failure reason, and the import continues.
- Progress and summary surfaced as an async job (`GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`) rendered on SCR-142.

## Out of scope
- Importing anything other than Bybit public trade archives (no third-party data, no book reconstruction).
- Backfilling bars from REST kline - that path belongs to E16-T04's gap backfill.
- A dedicated import screen; progress lives on SCR-142 (E16-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Import a date range
  Given the owner imports 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30 of BTCUSDT public trade archives
  When the job completes
  Then the files are downloaded, checksum-validated, converted and written to the cold tier
  And the summary reports files processed, rows written, rows discarded as overlap and files skipped

Scenario: Recorded data wins on overlap
  Given the recorder already covers 2026-06-20 to 2026-06-30 for BTCUSDT
  When the same range is imported
  Then no imported row for that window is written, the overlap is reported with its exact bounds, and no duplicate trade exists

Scenario: Corrupt file does not abort the import
  Given one file in the range fails its checksum
  Then that file is skipped and named in the summary and the remaining files are still imported

Scenario: Import is resumable
  Given the import is cancelled after 12 of 30 files
  When it is restarted with the same parameters
  Then it resumes at file 13 and does not re-download the first 12

Scenario: Imported windows are labelled archive-derived
  When coverage is requested over an imported-only window
  Then trades coverage is reported with source "archive" and orderbook_delta coverage is reported as absent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Archive URLs and file naming follow Bybit's public data site; the base URL is config (`CV_BYBIT_ARCHIVE_BASE`) so a layout change is a config fix, not a code change. Every URL is constructed from a validated symbol and an ISO date - never from user free text.
- Downloads go to a temp directory on the recording volume, are validated, converted, then moved into place atomically (write-temp-then-rename), so a crash never leaves a half file registered in a DuckDB view.
- Overlap detection queries `CoverageService` once per day-partition rather than per row.
- Conversion asserts the schema: columns, dtypes and monotonic `exch_ts` per file; a file whose timestamps fall outside its nominal date is skipped as corrupt.
- Error codes: `import_checksum_failed`, `import_parse_failed`, `import_range_invalid`.

## Test plan
- Unit: URL construction (including rejection of an unknown symbol), checksum validation, schema assertion, overlap arithmetic, checkpoint resume.
- Integration: import a 3-day fixture set (committed sample archives) into a clean cold tier; then re-import over a recorded window asserting recorded-wins and zero duplicates; then import with one deliberately corrupted file.
- Perf: importing one month of BTCUSDT trades keeps live ingest p95 lag unchanged.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Fetching remote archives is the epic's only outbound-network surface: enforce HTTPS, pin the host to the configured Bybit archive domain, cap decompressed size per file (zip-bomb guard, `CV_IMPORT_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_MB` default 2048), and validate every extracted path stays inside the temp directory (archive path traversal - the second half of the epic's named security concern in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md`). Requires `recording:write`. Imports are audited with symbol, range and byte count. **PR carries the `security` label.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A here; the progress UI (CMP-023 ProgressBar on SCR-142) is covered by E16-S04 and E16-D04.

## Performance notes
Bounded concurrency and bandwidth as above; the importer yields when `recorder_write_backlog_rows` is non-zero so live capture always wins.

## Observability
Metrics `import_files_total{result}`, `import_rows_written_total`, `import_rows_discarded_total{reason}`, `import_bytes_downloaded_total`, `import_duration_seconds`. Audit `import.performed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated with committed fixture archives.
- [ ] Zip-bomb and path-traversal guards tested explicitly.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] Security sign-off on the outbound-fetch and extraction paths.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T05` supplies the Parquet layout, watermark and DuckDB view registration this writes into.

title: Build SCR-140 recorder & storage screen with the recorded-symbol list
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-001** (recorded-symbols list), **US-REC-005** (disk budget display) and **US-REC-008** (recorder health and control) as screen **SCR-140** at route `/admin/recorder` (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`). This is the screen that makes the owner decision visible: nothing is recorded by default, and the cost of every symbol you add is stated on the same row as the switch that added it.

SCR-140 is also reached from onboarding step 4 (`docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`) and from the owner CTA on SCR-047, so it is the destination for every "you have no history because you never recorded this" moment in the product.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/admin/recorder` inside the web app, RBAC-gated (`recording:read` to view, `recording:write` for controls) using CMP-087 AdminLayout - **no separate admin app**.
- Header summary: symbols recording, total disk used, default retention, and the explicit statement that nothing is recorded by default when the list is empty.
- Symbol table (CMP-049 Table of CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow): symbol, since (first recorded timestamp), depth, measured GB/day, size, pin toggle, retention, state badge (recording / starting / degraded / paused / stopped / error) and, for auto-recorded rows, an explicit **auto-recorded** badge naming the trigger (chart open / position open).
- Controls: `+ Record a symbol` (CMP-055 FilterBar-driven symbol picker), start/stop, pin (keep forever), depth tier change, per-symbol retention, and the buttons `Retention policy` (opens SCR-141), `Compact now`, `Purge expired`.
- Disk meter (CMP-023 ProgressBar) with numeric text: used / cap, and the projection ("projection 60 d: 118 GB") plus days of runway.
- States: running · starting · degraded (gap count with timestamps) · paused · disk warning at 80% ("Disk 80% full - recording stops at 95% to protect the database") · disk critical (recording stopped banner) · purge in progress · **empty** (no symbols recorded yet, CMP-026 EmptyState).
- Live updates from the WS `recorder` topic at 1 Hz, falling back to `GET /recording/status` polling if the socket is down.
- Validation rules from the screen spec: stopping warns that history stops accumulating while existing data is retained per policy; a symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded ("SOLUSDT has an open position and is auto-recorded.").
- Analytics/audit triggers: `recorder.started|stopped|pinned|retention_changed|purged`.

## Out of scope
- The retention policy editor modal itself (E16-S03 / SCR-141) and the storage panel (E16-S04 / SCR-142) - this screen only links to them.
- Bulk import UI (E16-S04).
- Chart-side empty states (E16-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fresh install shows an honest empty state
  Given no symbols have ever been recorded
  When the owner opens /admin/recorder
  Then the empty state states that nothing is recorded by default, explains that history begins when recording begins, and offers a single primary action to record a symbol

Scenario: Adding a symbol reflects within 5 seconds
  When the owner adds BTCUSDT
  Then a row appears in state starting, transitions to recording within 5 seconds via the WS recorder topic, and shows its first-recorded timestamp

Scenario: Auto-recorded rows are labelled, not hidden
  Given SOLUSDT was auto-recorded because a chart is open
  Then its row carries an auto-recorded badge naming the trigger and a one-click stop control

Scenario: A symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded
  Given SOLUSDT has an open position
  When the owner attempts to stop recording it
  Then the action is refused with the message that the symbol has an open position and is auto-recorded

Scenario: Stopping explains the consequence before it happens
  When the owner stops recording ETHUSDT
  Then a confirmation states that history stops accumulating while existing data is retained per the retention policy, and only then is the stop sent

Scenario: Disk warning is visible and specific
  Given usage is at 82 percent of the configured cap
  Then a warning banner states that recording stops at 95 percent to protect the database, and the meter shows the numeric used-of-cap figure and the projected full date

Scenario: Viewer sees status but no controls
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the table and disk meter render read-only and every control is absent, with a sentence explaining that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: Socket loss degrades gracefully
  Given the WS connection drops
  Then the page falls back to polling, shows a last-updated timestamp, and never displays stale figures as live
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET /recording/status`, `GET /recording/symbols`, `GET /recording/storage`, `POST /recording/symbols`, `PATCH|DELETE /recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}`, `POST /recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}/pin`, `POST /admin/recorder/compact`, `POST /admin/recorder/purge`; live via WS topic `recorder`.
- Use the generated client from `packages/api-client` (E16-T08); no hand-written fetchers.
- The 1 Hz WS frame replaces the row model wholesale per symbol; row identity is `recordedSymbolId` so React reconciliation never re-mounts a row on a state change.
- Mutations are optimistic only for pin (cheap, reversible); start/stop/purge are pessimistic with a pending state, because pretending recording started when it did not is exactly the silent-failure class this epic exists to prevent.
- Purge from this screen routes through the confirmation flow specified for SCR-141/CMP-044 ConfirmDialog with the typed symbol echo.

## Test plan
- Unit (Vitest + RTL): row rendering per state, badge logic, refusal when a position is open, Viewer read-only rendering, fallback-to-polling behaviour.
- Storybook: CMP-177 states Recording, Stopped, Pinned, NearDiskBudget plus the screen's empty, warning and critical states; visual regression on each.
- Contract: MSW handlers generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; a response shape drift fails the suite.
- E2E (Playwright, added to the suite in E16-Q02): add symbol -> observe recording -> pin -> stop with confirmation -> empty state after removal.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the table and meter.
- Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This is an RBAC-gated admin surface inside the web app. Controls must be rendered from the session's permissions, never merely disabled client-side; the server enforces `recording:write` regardless (E16-T08). Purge additionally requires step-up - the UI must request elevation rather than assuming the session has it, and must never cache the elevated state. Do not render absolute host paths from `StorageUsage` to any role. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-140 and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: the disk meter carries numeric text (never colour alone); gaps are a real table with start/end/duration columns; state badges are text plus icon; the table is keyboard navigable with a visible focus ring; destructive controls are reachable by keyboard and their confirmation dialog traps focus and returns it on close; live 1 Hz updates use `aria-live="off"` on the table with a polite summary region announcing only material changes (a symbol entering error or the disk crossing a threshold), so a screen reader is not flooded once per second.

## Performance notes
Status updates at 1 Hz and the page never blocks ingestion (SCR-140 spec). Re-render budget: under 4 ms per frame for 20 rows; the meter and table are memoised on the symbol payload.

## Observability
Analytics `recorder.screen_viewed`; audit events are emitted server-side but the UI must surface their outcome (success/failure toast naming the symbol).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated.
- [ ] Storybook entries for every listed state; visual regression baselined.
- [ ] axe-core green; one manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design sign-off from E16-D02 checklist (all eight items) recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E16-Q01.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T08` (REST + WS contract and generated client), `E16-D06` (signed-off design and handoff), `E10` (app shell and routing), `E09` (auth, RBAC, step-up elevation).

## Branch
`feat/e16-recorder-screen` - split table and controls into 2 PRs to stay under 400 LOC.
