title: Surface recording status and auto-record triggers across chart and watchlist
body:
## Context
Implements the user-facing half of **US-REC-002** (auto-record triggers) and the recording-status element of **US-REC-006** outside the admin screen. ADR-0015 names the risk directly: auto-recording on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols, and the mitigation is "a visible recording indicator and a one-click stop" wherever the trigger happens - not buried on `/admin/recorder`.

Per the traceability matrix, US-REC-002 touches **SCR-041** (in-chart symbol/interval quick-switcher) and **SCR-100** (watchlist panel) as well as SCR-140; US-REC-006 touches **SCR-103** (symbol info / instrument detail), whose spec requires "recording status with a link to SCR-140 (owner)".

## Scope / Deliverables
- A shared `useRecordingStatus(symbol)` hook reading the WS `recorder` topic (one subscription per app, fanned out) so every surface shows the same state without N subscriptions.
- **SCR-041** quick-switcher: a compact recording dot per symbol row (recording / auto-recorded / not recorded) with a tooltip stating the reason and, for owners, a stop action.
- **SCR-100** watchlist (CMP-161/CMP-162 rows): the same indicator, plus an EmptyState (CMP-026) variant when no watchlist symbol is recorded that explains history will not exist for these symbols until recording starts.
- **SCR-103** symbol info: a recording-status block - state, first-recorded timestamp, size on disk, retention/pin - with a link to SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory sentence for Manager/Viewer.
- A non-modal, dismissible first-time notice when auto-record starts a symbol because a chart was opened: names the symbol, the trigger, the 60 s delay that already elapsed, and offers stop; shown at most once per session per symbol, never as a blocking dialog.
- Copy is taken verbatim from the signed-off design (E16-D05) - no ad-hoc strings.

## Out of scope
- Changing auto-record behaviour itself (E16-T02).
- The admin screen (E16-S01) and the chart empty states (E16-S05).
- Redesigning SCR-041/SCR-100/SCR-103 beyond adding these elements.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Auto-record is announced where it happens
  Given SOLUSDT is not recorded and the owner opens a chart for it
  When auto-record starts after the configured delay
  Then a dismissible notice names SOLUSDT, states that it started because a chart is open, and offers a one-click stop
  And the same notice is not shown again for SOLUSDT in this session

Scenario: Indicator agrees everywhere
  Given BTCUSDT is recording manually
  Then the quick-switcher, the watchlist row and the symbol-info block all show recording with reason manual, sourced from one subscription

Scenario: Non-owner sees status without controls
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the recording status is visible and the stop control is absent, replaced by a sentence stating that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: Watchlist of unrecorded symbols explains the consequence
  Given no watchlist symbol is recorded
  Then the panel shows the recording-not-started empty-state variant explaining that no history will exist for these symbols until recording begins

Scenario: Indicator is never colour-only
  When the recording indicator renders in any surface
  Then it carries accessible text or an accessible name stating the state, not merely a coloured dot
```

## Technical notes / design
- One app-level subscription to the `recorder` topic with all effective symbols; the hook selects by symbol from a context store so adding a fourth surface later costs nothing.
- The first-time notice is keyed `recorder.autostart.notice.<symbol>` in session storage; it is a toast-class element using the design-system notification primitive, never a modal, because it fires while the user is reading a chart.
- If the WS topic is unavailable, surfaces show an explicit unknown state rather than defaulting to "not recording" - showing "not recording" when we do not know is the same class of lie the epic is built to avoid.

## Test plan
- Unit: hook fan-out with one subscription and three consumers; indicator state mapping for all seven `recording_state` values plus unknown; once-per-session notice logic.
- Storybook: indicator in all states within each host component; the watchlist empty variant.
- E2E (in E16-Q02): open a chart for an unrecorded symbol with a shortened autostart delay, assert the notice and that stop works from the notice.
- a11y: axe-core on each host surface; screen-reader check that the indicator has an accessible name.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Recording state is not sensitive, but the stop control must be permission-gated client-side and enforced server-side (`recording:write`). The notice must not appear for roles that cannot act on it - a Viewer gets no stop affordance. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Indicator state is conveyed by accessible name plus shape/text, never colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The auto-start notice is `role="status"` (polite) not `role="alert"` - it must not interrupt, and it must be reachable and dismissible by keyboard. Tooltips have keyboard-accessible equivalents; the symbol-info block is plain text so it is fully readable by a screen reader.

## Performance notes
One WS subscription regardless of surface count; indicator re-render budget under 1 ms per row; the watchlist must not re-render wholesale on each 1 Hz frame (per-row memoisation keyed on state string).

## Observability
Analytics `recorder.autostart_notice_shown {symbol, trigger}` and `recorder.autostart_notice_stopped {symbol}` - a high stop rate is the signal that the delay or the trigger policy needs revisiting.

title: Build SCR-141 retention policy editor with destructive-change preview
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-003** (retention policy and pinning) as **SCR-141**, the modal that decides how long data lives. Its whole design problem is that shortening a number here destroys irreplaceable data, so the screen spec requires the consequence to be restated in text with the exact amount that becomes eligible for deletion, plus a typed confirmation for destructive reductions.

The dry-run preview the backend provides (E16-T06) is what makes this honest: the user sees exactly what would be deleted, by symbol, range and size, before anything is removed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Modal at SCR-141 using CMP-087 AdminLayout context, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Fields: global default retention days; per-tier rules for raw ticks, L2 deltas, bars and footprint aggregates; cold-tier migration age (QuestDB -> Parquet); per-symbol override table; pin-forever control per symbol.
- Live steady-state disk estimate under the chosen policy, recomputed as the user edits.
- Client validation mirroring the server: retention >= 1 day; raw-tick retention <= bar retention with the exact message "Bars can't be deleted before the ticks they came from are kept - adjust the tiers."
- **Preview before apply**: on submit, call the dry-run and render "this will delete N GB covering dates X-Y" per symbol and stream, listing protected items with their reason (pinned / leased / inside hot window). Nothing is applied until the user confirms.
- Typed confirmation for any reduction; `apply_now` checkbox that states changes otherwise take effect at the next nightly sweep.
- Compaction job state (queued / running / complete) shown after apply, since retention changes schedule background work rather than deleting synchronously.
- Unpin warning: unpinning states the exact volume that becomes eligible for deletion at the next pass (un-pinning never deletes retroactively).

## Out of scope
- Executing retention (E16-T06) and the purge flow (part of SCR-140, E16-S01).
- Postgres-side retention for OMS/journal tables.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduction shows the real cost before applying
  Given trades retention is 30 days
  When the owner reduces it to 7 and submits
  Then a preview lists, per symbol and stream, the exact GB and date range that would be deleted, and nothing is applied yet

Scenario: Typed confirmation gates destruction
  Given the preview shows data would be deleted
  When the owner confirms without typing the required confirmation text
  Then apply stays disabled and no request is sent

Scenario: Inverted tier retention is refused with a specific message
  When raw-tick retention is set above bar retention
  Then the form shows the message that bars cannot be deleted before the ticks they came from, and submit is disabled

Scenario: Pinned symbols are shown as protected
  Given BTCUSDT is pinned
  When any reduction is previewed
  Then BTCUSDT appears in the protected list with reason pinned and zero bytes deleted

Scenario: Unpinning warns with the exact volume
  When the owner unpins BTCUSDT
  Then the dialog states how many GB covering which dates become eligible for deletion at the next retention pass, and that nothing is deleted right now

Scenario: Apply schedules rather than blocks
  Given the owner applies a policy without apply_now
  Then a message states the change takes effect at the next nightly sweep, and the modal shows the queued job state

Scenario: Viewer cannot open the editor
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the retention policy entry point is not rendered and direct navigation is refused
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET|PUT /api/v1/recording/retention-policies` (with `?apply_now=`), the dry-run preview endpoint behind `PUT` validation, and `GET /recording/storage` for the steady-state estimate.
- The steady-state estimate is computed client-side from measured `daily_growth_bytes` per symbol times the chosen retention per stream - it is labelled an estimate, while the preview figures (server-side, measured) are labelled exact.
- The whole policy set is replaced atomically by the PUT; the form therefore submits the complete set, and a concurrent change by another session is detected by an ETag/If-Match round trip and surfaced as a conflict rather than silently overwriting.
- Error mapping: `retention_invalid_policy` -> field-level errors; `403` -> permission message; conflict -> reload-and-rebase prompt.

## Test plan
- Unit: validation matrix (all inversions, boundary 1 and 3650), estimate maths, confirmation gating, conflict handling.
- Storybook: default, with overrides, preview-with-deletions, preview-all-protected, conflict, and error states.
- Contract: MSW from the OpenAPI spec, including the 422 shape.
- E2E (E16-Q02): reduce retention, read the preview, cancel and assert nothing changed; then confirm and assert the policy persisted.
- a11y: axe-core; focus trap and return; every duration field states its unit.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This form authorises data destruction. Client controls are convenience only - the server validates and audits (`retention.change`, `retention.default_changed`, `retention.symbol_override_set`, `retention.pin_changed`). The UI must request step-up elevation where the backend requires it and must never retry a destructive PUT automatically on a network error (a silent retry could apply a policy the user cancelled). **Carries the `security` label; Security engineer reviews the confirmation and elevation flow.**

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-141: a form with a global default and a per-symbol override table; every duration field states its unit in an associated label, not a placeholder; the consequence of shortening retention is restated as text with the amount of data affected; the confirm dialog traps focus, is dismissible by Escape, and returns focus to the trigger; errors are associated with fields via `aria-describedby` and summarised at the top of the form for screen-reader users.

## Performance notes
Preview requests are debounced at 400 ms and cancelled on further edits; the modal must open in under 150 ms using cached policy data.

## Observability
Analytics `retention.editor_opened`, `retention.preview_requested`, `retention.change_cancelled_after_preview` (a high value here means the defaults are wrong). Audit events are server-side.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated.
- [ ] Storybook covers every listed state.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on the form and dialog.
- [ ] E16-D03 sign-off checklist (all six items) recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Security review of the destructive-confirmation flow signed off.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner.

title: Build SCR-142 storage panel with tier health, projections and import progress
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-004** (hot/cold tier management visibility), the projection half of **US-REC-005**, and **US-REC-007** (bulk backfill progress and summary) as **SCR-142**. The screen's job is to answer "where is my data, how fast is it growing, and what stops working first when the disk fills" - and the spec is explicit that recording pauses before trading is affected, and that this must be stated on screen, not merely implemented.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Page section at SCR-142 using CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-049 Table.
- Three tier tables - QuestDB hot, Parquet/DuckDB cold, Postgres - each with size, row counts by table, oldest/newest timestamps, health as text, and units on every figure.
- Growth and projection: daily growth per tier and per symbol (sparkline over the sampled series), projected full date, days of runway.
- Per-symbol breakdown for the hot tier.
- Operational state: ingestion lag, slowest queries, last vacuum/compaction, migration version and pending migrations (banner with the version delta when pending).
- Maintenance actions with progress and cancel: compact (`POST /admin/recorder/compact`), vacuum, tier migration - each an explicit action, each audited.
- Bulk archive import (US-REC-007): start an import for a symbol and date range, live progress, and the completion summary (files processed, rows written, overlap discarded, files skipped with reasons).
- States: healthy · migration pending · lag warning · read-only mode (disk full) · tier unreachable (error state per tier, not a whole-page failure).
- Low-disk warning and critical states drawn with the explicit statement of what stops working first: recording pauses before trading is affected.

## Out of scope
- The recorder symbol list (E16-S01) and retention editor (E16-S03).
- Backup/restore UI (platform/ops epic).
- Implementing compaction/import themselves (E16-T05, E16-T10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All three tiers are shown with units
  When the owner opens the storage panel
  Then QuestDB, Parquet/DuckDB and Postgres each show size, row counts, oldest and newest timestamps and a textual health state, every figure carrying its unit

Scenario: Projection is visible and sourced from measurement
  Then daily growth and the projected full date are shown per tier and per symbol, sourced from the sampled series rather than computed on request

Scenario: Disk pressure states what stops first
  Given usage is in the critical band
  Then the panel states that recording has paused and that trading is unaffected, naming the threshold that was crossed

Scenario: A tier being unreachable does not break the page
  Given the Parquet tier is unreachable
  Then that tier's card shows an error state with a retry, while the QuestDB and Postgres cards continue to render live figures

Scenario: Maintenance actions show progress and can be cancelled
  When the owner triggers compaction
  Then a job appears with queued, running and complete states and a cancel control, and the outcome is reported

Scenario: Import reports its summary honestly
  Given an import overlapping recorded data completes
  Then the summary states files processed, rows written, rows discarded as overlap and files skipped with their reasons
  And the imported range is labelled archive-derived with no book data

Scenario: Figures never silently go stale
  Given the 60 second sample has not refreshed for 5 minutes
  Then the panel shows a last-updated timestamp and a stale indicator rather than presenting old numbers as current
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` (server-sampled every 60 s per the screen spec), `POST /admin/recorder/compact`, the import job endpoints and `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` for progress.
- Polling at 60 s aligned to the server sample, with a manual refresh; no WS topic is required for this screen.
- Sparklines use CMP-024 over the persisted usage series; when fewer than 24 samples exist, render the "collecting data" variant rather than a misleading flat line.
- Long-running actions are jobs, not requests: the UI never blocks on compaction or import, and a page reload resumes progress from the job id.

## Test plan
- Unit: tier card rendering including the per-tier error state, stale detection, projection formatting, job progress state machine.
- Storybook: healthy, migration pending, lag warning, read-only/disk-full, tier unreachable, import running, import summary with skipped files.
- Contract: MSW from the OpenAPI `StorageUsage` schema.
- E2E (E16-Q02): trigger compaction and observe the job to completion; start a fixture import and read the summary.
- a11y: axe-core; all health states readable as text.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Performance notes
Storage figures are sampled server-side every 60 s and never computed on request (SCR-142 spec); heavy operations are explicit, cancellable actions with progress. The page renders in under 300 ms from cached data.

## Security notes
Read requires `recording:read`, maintenance actions require `recording:write` and are audited (`storage.compaction_triggered`, `storage.vacuum_triggered`, `storage.tier_migration_triggered`). The panel must not render absolute host filesystem paths or connection strings to any role - tier identity is a label, not a path. title: Implement recorder-dependent empty and partial-history states (SCR-047, SCR-151)
body:
## Context
Implements the UI half of **US-REC-006** and the empty-state half of **US-REC-005**. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §intro rule 3 makes this a product-wide contract: recorder-dependent emptiness is a *designed state*, never a blank canvas - every dependent surface shows "History starts <ts> - recording began then", with a CTA to SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory message otherwise.

This story ships **SCR-047** (chart empty / no-data) and the reusable **SCR-151** empty-state pattern with its `recording-not-started` variant, which E18 footprint, E19 profiles, E23 CVD and E26 replay all consume in R2. Building it once, correctly, here is what stops four later epics each inventing their own blank screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `CMP-026 EmptyState` gains the documented variants: `nothing-created-yet`, `no-match-for-filter`, `recording-not-started` - the third carrying the recording-start timestamp and a role-aware action.
- **SCR-047** chart empty/no-data state covering all four cases from the spec: symbol never recorded (offers live-only view and explains history starts when recording starts), interval too fine for available data, request window entirely before recording start, exchange returned no bars.
- Role-aware action: owner gets a real `Record this symbol` button wired to `POST /recording/symbols`; Manager/Viewer get an explanatory sentence, not a disabled button.
- **Partial history** treatment: when a requested range intersects `recording_gaps`, the covered part renders and the gap renders as a hatched, labelled region with its start, end and cause - never interpolated, never silently smoothed (ADR-0015 decision 7).
- Consumption of `GET /market/data-coverage` and of the `no_data_recorded` (422) error carrying `recording_started_at`, so the state is driven by data rather than by an empty array.
- Analytics `chart.empty_state_shown {reason}` and `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}`.
- Storybook documentation of the pattern so R2 epics adopt it without re-deriving it.

## Out of scope
- Footprint/profile/CVD/replay-specific gap rendering inside their own canvases (E18, E19, E23, E26) - they consume this pattern and component but own their draw calls.
- The recorder admin screens (E16-S01, S03, S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Never-recorded symbol explains rather than shows nothing
  Given SOLUSDT has never been recorded
  When a chart is opened for it
  Then the empty state states that there is no recorded history, notes that live data is streaming now, and shows a Record this symbol action for the owner

Scenario: Window before recording start is explained with the timestamp
  Given recording for BTCUSDT started 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC and a window before that is requested
  When the API returns 422 no_data_recorded
  Then the state states that no recorded history exists before that exact timestamp, rendered as text

Scenario: Non-owner gets an explanation, not a dead button
  Given a Viewer session on an unrecorded symbol
  Then no action button is rendered and a sentence explains that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: A gap is drawn as a gap
  Given the requested range contains a 12 minute recording gap
  Then the covered data renders, the gap renders as a hatched labelled region stating its start, end and cause, and no value is interpolated across it

Scenario: Kline-backfilled window is labelled as bar-derived
  Given part of a gap was backfilled from kline data
  Then those bars render with a bar-derived marker and the tick-level gap is still shown for tick-level views

Scenario: No infinite spinner
  Given the coverage request fails
  Then an error state with a retry is shown within 5 seconds, never a spinner that persists

Scenario: Empty chart costs no GPU
  When the chart empty state renders
  Then the GL context for the data layer is not initialised
```

## Technical notes / design
- Decision order for which state to show: coverage says nothing recorded -> `recording-not-started`; coverage exists but not in this window -> `no-data-in-range` with the nearest available range offered; instrument delisted/suspended -> instrument state; otherwise error.
- The empty state renders without initialising the GL data layer (SCR-047 performance rule), so it is a plain DOM overlay, not a GL scene.
- Gap regions are passed to the chart engine (E11) as an interval list on the render model; the engine draws the hatch, the story owns the labelling and the copy.
- Copy for all variants comes from the signed-off E16-D05 strings; every variant must name the cause, per the SCR-151 rule that "No data" alone is never acceptable.

## Test plan
- Unit: state-selection decision table (all four SCR-047 cases plus error), role-aware action rendering, timestamp formatting in the user's configured timezone.
- Storybook: every variant of CMP-026 and every SCR-047 case; visual regression baselined so R2 epics inherit a stable pattern.
- Integration: 422 `no_data_recorded` path end-to-end from the real endpoint.
- E2E (E16-Q02): open a chart for an unrecorded symbol as owner, use the CTA, and assert recording starts and the chart transitions out of the empty state.
- a11y: axe-core; screen-reader pass confirming heading + explanation + action structure.
- Perf: assert no GL context is created for the data layer in the empty state.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The empty state must not disclose whether *other* users recorded a symbol beyond what the role may see, and the CTA must be permission-gated (`recording:write`) with server-side enforcement. No host paths, no internal error text rendered verbatim to non-owners. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-047 and SCR-151: the empty state is a heading plus a paragraph plus an action - never an icon alone and never a bare "No data"; the recording-start timestamp is text, not an image or a tooltip; the CTA is a real button for owners and an explicit sentence for other roles; the hatched gap region has a text equivalent (a list of gap intervals with start, end and cause) reachable by keyboard, because a hatch pattern is invisible to a screen reader; contrast of the hatch meets 3:1 against the plot background.

## Performance notes
Empty states render without initialising heavy resources - no GL context, no subscriptions (SCR-151 rule) - so an empty panel costs nothing. State transition to a populated chart happens within one frame of data arriving.

## Observability
Analytics `chart.empty_state_shown {reason}` and `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` - used to find states users hit often and should not.

- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated including the no-GL-context assertion.
- [ ] CMP-026 variants documented in Storybook and added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` by PR.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on the gap text equivalent.

- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner and a design-system reviewer.

title: Write the black-box test plan for recorder lifecycle, retention and disk budget
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. E16 is unusually hard to test by inspection because most of its behaviour is temporal (grace periods, nightly jobs, 7-day projections) and destructive (retention, purge), so the plan must define how time is controlled and how destruction is verified without destroying a real dataset.

This ticket produces the plan that E16-Q02..Q06 execute against.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Test matrix dimensions: role (Owner / Manager / Viewer) x action (view, add, stop, pin, retention change, purge, compact, import) x state (empty, recording, degraded, disk-warning, disk-critical).
- Time-control strategy: a documented mechanism to advance the recorder's clock and trigger nightly jobs on demand in the test environment (`CV_TEST_CLOCK` hook), so a 30-day retention rule is verifiable in minutes without faking the production code path.
- Destructive-test protocol: every retention/purge case runs against a disposable dataset on a scratch volume, with a pre/post byte-and-row manifest so "nothing was deleted" and "exactly this was deleted" are both provable assertions rather than eyeball checks.
- Fixture catalogue: a seeded dataset with (a) a continuously recorded symbol, (b) a symbol with two known gaps of known causes, (c) a pinned symbol with data past every horizon, (d) an archive-imported-only range, (e) a symbol with an open position.
- Entry/exit criteria for QA sign-off of the epic, and the regression subset that must run on every later R2 epic that consumes recorded data.

```gherkin
Scenario: Time-dependent behaviour is testable in minutes
  When a case depends on a 30 day retention horizon or a 30 minute grace period

Scenario: The plan is reviewable by a developer who did not write it
  When a backend engineer reads a case cold
```

title: Automate the E2E suite for recorder lifecycle, retention and empty states
body:
## Context
The recorder's failures are quiet: a symbol that stops recording, a retention change that deletes more than the preview promised, an empty state that shows a blank chart instead of an explanation. These only surface end to end, across the WS topic, the REST surface and three screens. This ticket automates the cases the E16-Q01 plan marks as E2E-level, in Playwright against the web app and the Electron shell.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/recorder/`:
  1. `empty-install.spec.ts` - fresh install shows the empty recorder list and the honest empty state; nothing is recorded.
  2. `lifecycle.spec.ts` - add BTCUSDT, observe `starting -> recording` within 5 s via the WS-driven UI, verify first-recorded timestamp, pin, unpin with the warning, stop with the confirmation, verify data is retained.
  3. `auto-record.spec.ts` - with a shortened autostart delay, open a chart for an unrecorded symbol, assert the notice, stop from the notice; assert a symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded.
  4. `retention.spec.ts` - reduce retention, read the dry-run preview, cancel and prove nothing changed via the manifest, then confirm and prove exactly the previewed data was removed; assert the pinned symbol is untouched.
  5. `empty-states.spec.ts` - never-recorded chart, window-before-recording-start (422 path), partial-history gap hatch and its text equivalent, non-owner explanatory variants.
  6. `storage-panel.spec.ts` - trigger compaction and follow the job to completion; run a fixture archive import and assert the summary contents.
- Role coverage: each spec runs as Owner, and the permission-sensitive assertions additionally as Manager and Viewer.
- Runs in CI against a seeded stack using the E16-Q01 fixture catalogue and the `CV_TEST_CLOCK` hook; total wall time under 12 minutes.
- Electron shell run for `lifecycle` and `empty-states` (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` E2E requirement covering both web and Electron).

## Out of scope
- Unit and contract tests (owned by the implementing tickets).
- Performance, chaos and a11y automation (E16-Q04, E16-Q05).
- Exploratory testing (E16-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite is deterministic
  Given the suite runs 10 consecutive times in CI
  Then it passes 10 times with no retries and no fixed sleeps longer than 1 second

Scenario: Retention preview matches reality byte for byte
  When the retention spec applies a reduction after previewing it
  Then the post-state manifest differs from the pre-state manifest by exactly the previewed symbols, ranges and byte counts

Scenario: Pinned data survives every destructive case
  When every destructive spec has run
  Then the pinned symbol fixture is byte-identical to its pre-suite manifest

Scenario: Role assertions hold
  Given the suite runs as Viewer
  Then every write control is absent from the DOM, not merely disabled, and direct API calls from the page are refused
```

title: Run the exploratory charter for recorder surprise, honesty and data-loss traps
body:
## Context
Scripted tests verify what we thought of. The recorder's real risks are the things we did not: a user who browses 40 symbols in five minutes and finds 40 recordings running; a retention change applied while a replay is reading; a pin toggled twice quickly; a purge started, cancelled and restarted. ## Scope / Deliverables

  2. **Honesty charter** - can the UI ever show data that is not there, or hide data that is? Gap boundaries, partial history at the edge of a window, timezone boundaries, imported archive ranges presented as full history, stale figures presented as live, coverage after a purge.
  3. **Data-loss charter** - can a user destroy data without understanding they were about to? Double-clicks on destructive controls, browser back during a purge, concurrent retention edits from two sessions, unpin followed immediately by a nightly sweep, cancelled compaction.

title: Build the recorder perf, soak and disk-pressure chaos scripts
body:
## Context
Two of this epic's headline claims are numeric and one is behavioural: the recorder sustains live ingest without dropping messages, storage grows at the measured rate, and the disk-pressure ladder degrades exactly as ADR-0015 decision 6 specifies. ADR-0015's own Validation section names the disk-pressure chaos test (fill to 85%, 91%, 96% and assert each documented behaviour including pinned survival), and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-154 requires chaos coverage of DB unavailability and disk-full with the system failing closed on the order path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Soak script** (`perf/recorder/soak.py`): 24-hour continuous recording of 2 symbols at depth 200 against a replayed or live feed, asserting zero dropped messages, backlog p95 of 0, spill bytes 0, and GB/day within 20% of the E16-K01 measurement.
- **Ingest load script** (`perf/recorder/ingest_load.py`): synthetic 50k msg/s for 10 minutes, asserting p95 flush < 50 ms and memory ceiling 512 MiB.
- **API/WS load** (k6, `perf/recorder/api_load.js`): 5 concurrent `recorder` WS subscribers plus 1 Hz `/recording/status` polling plus coverage queries, asserting API p95 < 150 ms and frame size < 8 KiB for 20 symbols.
- **Disk-pressure chaos** (`chaos/recorder/disk_pressure.py`): a loopback volume filled to 76%, 81%, 91% and 96%, asserting at each step: warning event with suggested actions; auto-record refusal while explicit-list symbols keep recording; accelerated reaper below 15% free; ingestion pause for non-pinned auto symbols below 5% free; **pinned data byte-identical throughout**; and **order placement still succeeds at every level**.
- **DB-unavailability chaos** (`chaos/recorder/questdb_down.py`): stop QuestDB for 2 minutes and assert WAL spill then clean replay with no duplicates and no gap; then exhaust the WAL and assert an explicit `backpressure_drop` gap plus a critical event.
- **Roll-off interruption chaos**: kill the roll-off job between write and verify, and between verify and drop; assert no data loss and convergence on re-run.
- Results published to the CI perf trend so regressions in later epics are visible, with thresholds failing the build.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E16-Q02) and a11y (E16-Q05).
- Chart-engine FPS benchmarks (E11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Soak proves no silent loss
  Given a 24 hour soak at depth 200 on two symbols
  Then dropped messages are zero, spill bytes are zero, recorded rows reconcile with produced events, and measured GB/day is within 20 percent of the E16-K01 figure

Scenario: Disk ladder behaves exactly as specified at every level
  When the volume is filled to 76, 81, 91 and 96 percent in turn
  Then each documented behaviour occurs at its threshold, pinned data is byte-identical at the end, and an order placed at 96 percent still succeeds

Scenario: Database outage costs latency not history
  Given QuestDB is stopped for 2 minutes under live load
  Then events spill to the WAL and replay cleanly with no duplicates and no recorded gap
  And when the WAL is exhausted, a backpressure_drop gap covering exactly the dropped window is written and a critical event fires

Scenario: Interrupted roll-off never loses data
  Given the roll-off job is killed between write and verify
  Then the hot partition still exists, the partial Parquet file is quarantined, and a re-run completes correctly

Scenario: Thresholds gate the build
  Given a change regresses p95 flush beyond 50 milliseconds
  Then the perf job fails rather than merely recording a slower number
```

## Technical notes / design
- The loopback volume is created per run with `fallocate` + a filesystem image so fills are fast, repeatable and cannot touch the host's real disk; the harness refuses to run if the target path is not a loopback mount.
- Synthetic load reuses the E08 normaliser to generate realistic message mixes (trade bursts, depth churn, liquidation cascades) rather than uniform traffic, because the p95 that matters is the cascade.
- Reconciliation oracle: produced-event counter in the generator versus rows in QuestDB plus rows accounted for by gap records - the three must sum exactly.
- Runs nightly, not per PR, except the 10-minute ingest load which is cheap enough for the pipeline.

## Test plan
Self-verifying, with a deliberate negative control: run the disk-pressure suite against a build with the pin predicate removed and confirm the suite fails, proving the assertions have teeth.

## Security notes
Directly validates SR-096 (storage guard, recording volume separate, trading functional when the recording volume is full) and SR-154 (chaos coverage). Results are evidence for the E16-X02 security review and for the pre-Live pen-test scope.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: 50k msg/s ingest, p95 flush < 50 ms, 512 MiB queue ceiling, API p95 < 150 ms, WS frame < 8 KiB/20 symbols, storage growth within 20% of measurement (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #12 and the API/WS budgets).

## Observability
The harness scrapes the recorder metrics and attaches the Grafana snapshot to each run, so a failure comes with the panel that explains it.

- [ ] Nightly CI job green; thresholds enforced.
- [ ] Negative control performed and recorded.
- [ ] Results for the first full run recorded on this ticket and referenced from the epic.

title: Run the accessibility audit for the recorder screens and empty-state pattern
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; automated checks catch roughly a third of what matters here. E16's specific risks are unusual: a table that updates once per second can flood a screen reader, a hatched gap region is invisible to one, and a disk meter conveyed by colour alone would hide the single most important number on the screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Manual audit of SCR-140, SCR-141, SCR-142, SCR-047 and the SCR-151 pattern instances shipped by E16-S05, against WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS, covering: the recorder table and its 1 Hz updates, the disk meter's numeric text, the retention form and its confirmation dialog, the storage panel's tier tables and progress bars, the empty states, and the gap-interval text equivalent.
- Keyboard-only pass: every control reachable and operable, visible focus throughout, focus trapped and returned by dialogs, no keyboard trap in the symbol picker.
- Contrast verification for state badges, the hatch pattern against the plot background (>=3:1 for non-text), meter fills, and disabled states.
- Zoom/reflow at 200% and 400% per WCAG 1.4.10, and `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for any progress animation.
- Findings filed with severity and the specific success criterion; a written audit report at `docs/qa/a11y/e16-recorder-audit.md` with a pass/fail per screen and per criterion.
- axe-core CI assertions added for all five surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Fixing findings - they are filed against the owning story or as new tickets.
- The design-level a11y review, which happened pre-build in E16-D06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live updates do not flood assistive technology
  Given a screen reader is active on the recorder table with 20 symbols updating at 1 Hz
  Then routine value changes are not announced, and only material changes such as a symbol entering error or the disk crossing a threshold are announced politely

Scenario: The gap is perceivable without sight
  Given a chart shows a hatched recording gap
  When a screen-reader user navigates the chart region
  Then a text equivalent lists the gap start, end and cause, reachable by keyboard

Scenario: No information is conveyed by colour alone
  When every state badge, meter and health indicator is inspected
  Then each carries text or an accessible name in addition to colour, and contrast meets AA

Scenario: Destructive dialogs are safe from the keyboard
  When the retention confirmation dialog opens
  Then focus moves into it, is trapped, Escape cancels without applying, and focus returns to the trigger

Scenario: Reflow holds at 400 percent
  When each screen is zoomed to 400 percent at 1280 pixels wide
  Then no horizontal scrolling of content is required and no content is lost or overlapped

Scenario: Audit is auditable
  When the report is published
  Then it records tool versions, assistive-technology versions, the criteria checked and a pass or fail per screen with evidence
```

## Technical notes / design
- axe-core runs against each screen in its populated, empty, warning and error states - an empty state is where a11y regressions hide, since it is rarely screenshotted.
- The 1 Hz announcement rule is verified by recording the screen-reader speech stream for 60 seconds and counting utterances; more than a handful is a fail.
- Contrast measured with a sampling tool on rendered pixels, not on token values, because the hatch is a composited pattern.

## Context

The subsystem is unusual in that its worst outcomes are not confidentiality breaches but availability and integrity ones: filling the disk takes trading down, and silently deleting or misreporting history corrupts every analysis built on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Threat model document `docs/security/threat-models/e16-recorder.md` covering components `RecordingPolicy`, `StreamWriter`, `RetentionManager`, `RollOffJob`, `DiskBudget`, the archive importer, the `recording` REST surface and the `recorder` WS topic, with a data-flow diagram and trust boundaries consistent with `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4.
- STRIDE enumeration per component with likelihood, impact, rating, existing control, residual risk. Mandatory coverage of at least:
  - **S** - forged auto-record trigger (a chart-open signal for a symbol the actor cannot otherwise record).
  - **T** - retention policy or gap-metadata tampering making absent data look present; archive file substitution during import.
  - **R** - deletion without an attributable audit entry; audit entry lost because the data it described was deleted first.
  - **I** - storage responses leaking host filesystem paths, volume names or other users' recorded symbols to a Viewer.
  - **D** - disk exhaustion by rapid chart opening or by a large import; WAL exhaustion; reaper starvation by a permanently held read lease.
  - **E** - Viewer or Manager reaching `recording:write` or purge without step-up; `CV_TEST_CLOCK` or `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` reachable in production.
- Abuse-case catalogue with a concrete attack narrative and an expected system response for each, written so QA can execute them directly (handed to E16-Q01).
- Mapping of every threat to an existing control (SR-096, SR-125, SR-154, permission 51) or to a new requirement raised as a ticket against the owning E16 task.
- Data classification statement for every store E16 writes: recorded market data (**public** content, **internal** operational metadata), coverage/gap metadata (**internal**, integrity-critical), audit entries (**internal**, tamper-evident).

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls - findings become work on E16-T02/T03/T05/T06/T07/T08/T10.
- The security review of the shipped code (E16-X02) and the pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  When the model is reviewed
  Then each of the eight named components has a STRIDE row per applicable category with a rating and a named control or an open finding

Scenario: The Critical DoS has a tested control
  Given threat S2 disk exhaustion is rated Critical
  Then it maps to SR-096 and to the disk-pressure chaos test in E16-Q04, with the acceptance thresholds stated

Scenario: Path traversal is modelled at every write and delete site
  When archive import, Parquet export and Parquet deletion are analysed
  Then each has an explicit containment requirement and a corresponding test referenced

Scenario: Findings become work, not prose
  Given a threat with no adequate existing control
  Then a ticket is raised against the owning E16 task and linked from the model, and the model records the ticket key

Scenario: The model is signed off
  When the review meeting concludes
  Then the Security engineer, the Architect and the backend lead have approved, and residual risks are listed with an accepting owner
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use the same table format as the existing §5 areas in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so the model can be folded back into the security program document rather than living apart from it.
- Attacker model: the product is Tailscale-only with three roles, so the realistic adversaries are (a) a lower-privileged authenticated user (Viewer/Manager), (b) a compromised browser session, (c) a malicious or corrupted remote archive, (d) an operational mistake by the Owner. The model's abuse cases are executed by E16-Q01/Q02/Q04. This ticket verifies itself by review: every abuse case must be executable as written, checked by the QA lead during sign-off.

This ticket is the security work. Its output gates E16-X02 and feeds the pre-Live pen-test scope in E43. Classification of the document itself: internal.

title: Security review: destructive paths, RBAC, path containment, config gating
body:
## Context
E16 ships the product's first irreversible data-destruction path and its first outbound file fetch. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §14.8 defines a dedicated review checklist for data/recorder/export tickets, including the explicit item "disk-budget guard tested: at 90% usage recording pauses and trading remains fully functional (SR-096)". This ticket is the white-box review that signs that checklist off against the code that actually shipped, not against the design.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Manual code review of `recorder/policy.py`, `writer.py`, `sessions.py`, `rolloff.py`, `retention.py`, `budget.py`, `importer.py` and the `recording` route layer, against the E16-X01 model and the §14.8 checklist.
- Focus areas, each with a written finding or an explicit pass:
  1. **Destructive-path authorization** - purge requires `recording:write` **and** step-up elevation (permission 51), a mandatory reason and an exact `confirm_symbol` echo; the pin predicate is the reaper's first predicate; `applies_to_pinned` cannot be set without elevation.
  2. **Audit completeness and ordering** - an audit entry is written before and after every delete, survives the deleted data, and is hash-chained per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10.
  3. **Path containment** - every Parquet write, delete, archive extraction and quarantine path is resolved and asserted inside its configured root; symlinks refused; no user-supplied path reaches the filesystem from the API (`archive_path` is server-config only).
  4. **Outbound fetch hardening** - HTTPS enforced, host pinned to the configured Bybit archive domain, decompressed-size cap, extraction path validation, no redirect to a different host.
  5. **Resource limits** - `CV_RECORDER_MAX_SYMBOLS`, WAL bound, import concurrency/bandwidth caps, and the disk ladder all present and not bypassable by an auto-record path.
  6. **Config gating** - `CV_TEST_CLOCK` and `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` cannot be enabled in a production build; volume-separation assertion runs at startup.
  7. **Information exposure** - no absolute host path, connection string or internal error text reaches a non-owner role in any response or UI string.
  8. **Idempotency** - compact and purge require `Idempotency-Key`; a retry cannot double-purge.
- Semgrep/Bandit rules added under `ci/semgrep/recorder.yml` codifying the repeatable checks: filesystem write with a non-validated path, `tarfile`/`zipfile` extraction without member validation, subprocess use in the recorder package, and destructive SQL (`DROP PARTITION`, directory unlink) outside `retention.py`.
- ZAP/DAST profile additions for the `recording` and `/admin/recorder/*` endpoints, exercising the role matrix and the purge refusal paths.
- Review record at `docs/security/reviews/e16-recorder-review.md` with the §14.8 checklist completed item by item.

## Out of scope
- Fixing findings (raised against the owning ticket).
- The pen-test itself (E43, pre-Live).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every checklist item is answered with evidence
  When the review record is published
  Then every item of 04-security-program.md section 14.8 has a pass or a finding, each citing a file, line and test

Scenario: Purge cannot be reached without elevation
  Given a session with recording:write but no step-up elevation
  When purge is invoked directly against the API
  Then it is refused with 403 and the attempt is audited, verified by both code review and a DAST case

Scenario: Path traversal is impossible at every site
  Given crafted symbol, date and archive member values containing traversal sequences
  When export, delete, import and quarantine paths are constructed
  Then every one resolves inside its root or raises, proven by a test per site

Scenario: Test-only config cannot ship
  Given a production build
  When CV_TEST_CLOCK is set
  Then the application refuses to start or ignores it, and the review records which

Scenario: New SAST rules catch a planted defect
  Given a branch that writes a Parquet file using an unvalidated path
  Then the semgrep rule fails the build

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  When the review concludes
  Then every finding has a severity, an owning ticket, and either a fix or an Owner-accepted risk
```

## Technical notes / design
- Review is code-reading plus targeted dynamic probes, not a scan-and-forget: for each focus area, the reviewer writes the adversarial input that should fail and confirms it does.
- The planted-defect check for the new SAST rules is mandatory - a rule that has never failed has never been shown to work.
- DAST runs against a seeded scratch environment; destructive cases run only where a purge is expected to succeed, and the fixture is restored afterwards.

## Test plan
- The dynamic probes become permanent tests in the owning packages, so the review's findings do not regress silently.
- Semgrep rules ship with positive and negative fixtures under `ci/semgrep/tests/`.
- DAST profile runs in the nightly security job.
